- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.  
- Model consistently overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3–5 days); apply a 1–2 point downward correction to prevent overshoot.  
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward sentiment trends; add 0.5–1.5 points to forecast to account for mean reversion toward prior levels.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags by 1–3 days in capturing sentiment-driven reversals; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shifts.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with the most recent sentiment; prioritize recent sentiment over historical trends.
